Session Management: How Websites Remember You: storyboard

Episode 10 · voice Matilda · 9 scenes · 85.5s (measured timing) · one still per beat, 8 frames after it fires

hook hook Hook · 0.0s–8.7s

Headline: Total amnesia

“With every single click, a website forgets who you are, and yet somehow it still knows you're logged in. So how?”

branding sting 8.7s–10.2s

Bite wipe → logos → cut. No voiceover, just the chomp.

idea idea Diorama · 10.2s–18.3s

Headline: Ticket, please

“The trick is a coat check: you hand over your coat once, get a numbered ticket back, and from then on you just show the ticket.”

breakdown login Sequence · 18.3s–28.7s

No headline

“Logging in is handing over the coat: the server checks your password once, saves your session, and gives your browser a cookie holding just the ticket number.”

breakdown rides Sequence · 28.7s–38.9s

Headline: Shown every visit

“That cookie rides along on every request, and the server checks the ticket against its store, usually Redis or a database, so no password is needed.”

breakdown tokens Split · 38.9s–49.8s

Headline: Store or carry?

“Tokens skip the store: your browser carries your details itself, signed so they can't be faked. No lookup, but no easy way to cancel one early.”

breakdown lifecycle StateMachine · 49.8s–59.2s

No headline

“Either way, every session needs an ending: it expires when you go idle, dies when you log out, and swaps to a fresh ID at login.”

breakdown flags Snippet · 59.2s–71.2s

Headline: Three little flags

“The cookie carrying that ID needs locks too: HttpOnly hides it from scripts, Secure sends it only over HTTPS, and SameSite keeps other sites from using it.”

breakdown bigpicture BigPicture · 71.2s–79.4s

No headline

“So all of it adds up to one simple ticket: checked on every visit, with an expiry date, and a lock to keep it safe.”

gist gist GistCard · 79.4s–85.5s

No headline

“That's the gist: a session is a ticket, not your password. Follow for more.”
